system.name: ONCache
system.one_liner: a cache-based container overlay network that rewrites packet headers, instead of encapsulating them, to cut per-packet overhead

content.subject: how a container packet's IP/MAC header fields are rewritten to host addresses on egress and restored on ingress

elements.name: Payload
elements.role: the unchanged upper-layer payload (TCP/UDP/ICMP...) carried through all three stages

elements.name: IP Header
elements.role: the packet's IP header field, whose addresses are rewritten and restored

elements.name: MAC Header
elements.role: the packet's MAC header field, whose addresses are rewritten and restored

elements.name: Container IP addresses
elements.role: the original IP header content, present in the original and restored packets

elements.name: Host IP addresses & Restore key
elements.role: the masqueraded IP header content, carrying the host's address plus a key used to restore the original later

elements.name: Container MAC addresses
elements.role: the original MAC header content, present in the original and restored packets

elements.name: Egress-Prog
elements.role: the eBPF/tc program that masquerades the packet on the way out of the container

elements.name: Ingress-Prog
elements.role: the eBPF/tc program that restores the packet on the way into the destination container

relations.what: Egress-Prog rewrites the IP/MAC headers to host addresses plus a restore key
Ingress-Prog rewrites the host header fields back to the original container addresses using the restore key

panels.label: (a) Original Packet
panels.differs: template: payload plus IP/MAC headers carrying the container's own addresses

panels.label: (b) Masqed Packet
panels.differs: the IP and MAC header rows (highlighted green/orange) are rewritten to host IP/MAC addresses plus a restore key, produced by Egress-Prog

panels.label: (c) Restored Packet
panels.differs: the IP and MAC headers are rewritten back to the original container addresses by Ingress-Prog, restoring the packet to its (a) state

values.what: the concrete header field contents at each stage: container IP/MAC addresses versus host IP/MAC addresses plus a restore key
values.linked_by: position (same IP Header / MAC Header row across all three packet frames) and colour (rewritten fields highlighted)
values.result_cells: the (c) Restored Packet frame shows the final result, matching (a) exactly

content.key_idea: The rewriting-based tunneling protocol substitutes traditional outer-header encapsulation with in-place rewriting of the container's own IP/MAC header fields to host addresses (plus a restore key) on egress, then rewrites them back to the original container addresses on ingress at the destination.
content.reading_order: left to right through the three frames (a) Original, (b) Masqed, (c) Restored, following the Egress-Prog and Ingress-Prog arrows between them

palette.used_for: light green fill of the IP Header row across all three packet frames
light orange fill of the MAC Header row across all three packet frames
light grey fill of the Payload row
gold stroke accents on the MAC Header box and Egress/Ingress-Prog icons
green stroke accents on the IP Header box

style.stroke: thin (~0.7pt) black box outlines, grey (#666666) for secondary lines
style.arrows: thin black arrows between the three packet frames, each labelled with a small gear/program icon (Egress-Prog, Ingress-Prog)
style.font: Arial sans, ~6-7.5pt, italic for the rewritten field descriptions
style.icons: a small gear-like icon on the Egress-Prog / Ingress-Prog arrows

encoding.color_means: green = IP Header row, orange = MAC Header row, grey = unchanged Payload row, consistent across all three frames so the reader can track each field
encoding.line_style_means: solid arrows only; no dashed lines are used
encoding.state_means: before/after states are told apart by the italic field-content text inside each row (container addresses vs host addresses/restore key) while the row layout and colour stay identical across frames
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; the Egress-Prog/Ingress-Prog labels on the connecting arrows name the operation that produced each transition
encoding.emphasis: keeping the payload row visually unchanged across all three frames isolates attention on just the IP/MAC header rows that the protocol rewrites
reusable_patterns: three identical stacked-header frames in a row, connected by named-operation arrows, with only the rewritten rows' text changing

evidence: substituting the encapsulation of outer headers in traditional tunneling protocols, with the rewriting of inner headers

summary: This figure from ONCache's appendix on its rewriting-based tunneling protocol shows how a container packet's headers change along the data path. Frame (a) is the Original Packet as sent by the container: a Payload row plus IP Header and MAC Header rows carrying the container's own addresses. An Egress-Prog operation transforms it into frame (b), the Masqed Packet, where the IP and MAC Header rows are rewritten to host IP/MAC addresses together with a restore key, while the Payload is untouched. An Ingress-Prog operation at the destination then transforms it into frame (c), the Restored Packet, rewriting the header rows back to the original container addresses. The three frames share an identical stacked-header layout and colour coding (green IP Header, orange MAC Header, grey Payload), so only the header text changes are visible, illustrating that this tunneling approach avoids adding any outer encapsulation headers.
